strings.return.campaign.description: A homecoming in three acts: arrival, reality, and the difficult art of actually staying.
strings.return.campaign.title: Return
strings.return.city_return_1.listen: Answer every question without performing expat expertise
strings.return.city_return_1.push: Explain how customs works 'where you were'
strings.return.city_return_1.text: The customs officer studies the espresso machine in your luggage as though it has personally applied for citizenship.
strings.return.city_return_2.text: Your first landlord quotes the rent in euros and the nostalgia in leva. The apartment has a view of three separate parking disputes.
strings.return.city_return_3.favour: Call in the favour you earned
strings.return.city_return_3.favour_fail: No one owes you that favour yet.
strings.return.city_return_3.text: An old colleague offers introductions, quiet warnings, and a desk that becomes available the moment its current owner finally moves the printer.
strings.return.city_return_4.ending_becomes_the_: The One Who Actually Knows How Things Work
strings.return.city_return_4.text: A month later the city no longer feels foreign, which is not remotely the same thing as feeling easy. You decide what returning is actually going to mean.
strings.return.city_return_event_1.text: The day contributes its own amendment.
strings.return.city_return_event_1a.text: The luggage slip gets you through a second inspection in twelve flat seconds.
strings.return.city_return_event_1b.text: A shift change restarts the entire conversation, now with chairs and considerably less patience.
strings.return.city_return_event_2.text: A seeded interruption arrives on schedule.
strings.return.city_return_event_2a.proceed: Meet the old colleague for coffee
strings.return.city_return_event_2a.text: Your colleague remembers the one clerk in the whole building who still answers email.
strings.return.city_return_event_2b.text: The cheaper flat is real; the bathroom is best described as an interpretive proposal.
strings.return.ending_becomes_the_local_expert.t:
The One Who Actually Knows How Things Work

Word spreads that you can navigate both worlds. Friends start forwarding you their parents' paperwork, their cousins' visa questions, their own confused feelings about leaving. You become, unofficially, the neighbourhood's foreign office.
strings.return.ending_becomes_the_new_elder.text:
The Person Who Actually Answers Questions Now

Somewhere between fixing the well and mediating the fence dispute, you become the person the village calls first. Nobody voted on this. It happened anyway.
strings.return.ending_city_with_open_eyes.text:
The Sceptical Returner

You stay without pretending the city is perfect, or that abroad ever quite was either.
strings.return.ending_commutes_between_two_lives:
A Life With Two Departure Boards

You never fully choose. Flights get booked, the hotel keeps a room ready, and eventually the receptionist stops asking when you're leaving — she just asks which terminal.
strings.return.ending_exhausted_departure.text:
The Open Return Ticket

You leave exhausted, keeping the key anyway. Some decisions need distance before they become answers.
strings.return.ending_home_again.text:
Home Again

The questions become routine, the advice ambient, and even the mechanic's recommendation useful. You stay.
strings.return.ending_married_into_staying.text:
An Aunt's Plan, Executed Flawlessly

The 'coffee with a family friend' your aunt arranged turns out to be exactly what it looked like. You are still slightly annoyed about the manipulation. You are also, undeniably, staying.
strings.return.ending_opens_a_business_out_of_sp:
Out of Sheer Stubbornness

Tired of explaining why 'it's just different abroad,' you open a small business built entirely on doing one thing properly. It survives, mostly on the reputation of being the one place in the neighbourhood that answers the phone.
strings.return.ending_optimistic_return.text:
The Returner

You build a life from old streets and new boundaries. Home becomes a verb again, slowly, on its own schedule.
strings.return.ending_rakia_diplomacy.text:
Settled Over Rakia

A boundary dispute that has run for three generations ends over a bottle of the neighbour's homemade rakia and a hand-drawn map, redrawn this time by consensus.
strings.return.ending_reverse_culture_shock_wins:
You Book the Return Flight

Six months in, you realize you miss the queue discipline, the weather complaints, and, inexplicably, the customer service. You book a one-way ticket back and tell everyone it's temporary.
strings.return.ending_settled_in_the_village.tex:
A Light in the Village

You stay. The roof holds, the neighbours knock, and the silence finally includes you.
strings.return.ending_the_key_gets_lost.text:
The Apartment You Never Quite Took

You misplace the key somewhere between two airports and three time zones. Nobody mentions it again, which somehow feels worse than if they had.
strings.return.ending_village_adopts_you_as_proj:
The Whole Village Renovates Your Roof

Word gets around that you're 'the one who came back.' Within a week, half the village has an opinion about your roof and a third of them show up to fix it, unasked, for lunch and gossip.
strings.return.ending_winter_defeats_you.text:
One Winter Was Enough

The wood runs out in February, the road ices over, and the nearest working shop is forty minutes away with chains on the tyres. You leave before spring, quietly, and don't quite explain why.
strings.return.expat_returns.choice_accept_desti: Accept your destiny and stay in the city
strings.return.expat_returns.choice_explain: Explain nothing; take the village road
strings.return.expat_returns.choice_laugh: Laugh and book a room for one more week
strings.return.expat_returns.choice_smile: Smile and try the city again
strings.return.expat_returns.text: After years abroad, you land at Sofia Airport with two suitcases and a theory that coming home will be simpler than leaving was. Customs, family, and the taxi rank outside have all prepared counterarguments.
strings.return.temporary_return_1.text: The hotel receptionist recognizes your accent, silently upgrades her opinion of you, and asks — not unkindly — when exactly you're leaving again.
strings.return.temporary_return_2.text: Family lunches expand to occupy every decision you had quietly postponed while abroad.
strings.return.temporary_return_3.favour: Call in the favour you earned
strings.return.temporary_return_3.favour_fail: No one owes you that favour yet.
strings.return.temporary_return_3.text: A return ticket sits open in your inbox while an aunt calmly leaves a spare apartment key beside your coffee, saying nothing.
strings.return.temporary_return_4.ending_commute: A Life With Two Departure Boards
strings.return.temporary_return_4.ending_the_key: The Apartment You Never Quite Took
strings.return.temporary_return_4.text: The final morning arrives without resolving whether departure is failure, wisdom, or simply one more route home.
strings.return.temporary_return_event_1.text: The day contributes its own amendment.
strings.return.temporary_return_event_1a.text: The old hotel ledger still carries your family's name, from a wedding in 1986.
strings.return.temporary_return_event_1b.text: A conference fills the hotel and quietly relocates you to a room above the kitchen.
strings.return.temporary_return_event_2.text: A seeded interruption arrives on schedule.
strings.return.temporary_return_event_2a.text: The apartment is small, sunny, and legally entangled only in the ordinary, survivable ways.
strings.return.temporary_return_event_2b.text: The taxi driver delivers a complete economic forecast before you even reach the ring road.
strings.return.var_connections.label: Old Connections
strings.return.var_preparation.label: Local Knowledge
strings.return.var_pressure.label: Homesickness
strings.return.village_return_1.listen: Listen to the neighbour's full history
strings.return.village_return_1.push: Start repairs before anyone can advise you
strings.return.village_return_1.text: The village house is beautiful from the road and urgently educational from inside. A neighbour arrives before the electricity does, carrying opinions and a flashlight.
strings.return.village_return_2.prepare: Check the deeds before the roof
strings.return.village_return_2.text: The well works, the roof mostly works, and four relatives disagree, at volume, about which wall technically belongs to whom.
strings.return.village_return_3.favour: Call in the favour you earned
strings.return.village_return_3.favour_fail: No one owes you that favour yet.
strings.return.village_return_3.text: You trade a full day of clearing weeds for a hand-drawn map of pipes, boundaries, and several decades of grudges.
strings.return.village_return_4.ending_becomes_t: The Person Who Actually Answers Questions Now
strings.return.village_return_4.ending_village_a: The Whole Village Renovates Your Roof
strings.return.village_return_4.text: Winter makes the village honest. The quiet is generous; the distance to literally everything is not.
strings.return.village_return_event_1.text: The day contributes its own amendment.
strings.return.village_return_event_1a.text: The map reveals a stopcock hidden beneath a plum tree under two decades of leaves.
strings.return.village_return_event_1b.proceed: Follow the pipe that sounds least theoretical
strings.return.village_return_event_1b.text: The first pipe you touch introduces itself by flooding the pantry with real enthusiasm.
strings.return.village_return_event_2.text: A seeded interruption arrives on schedule.
strings.return.village_return_event_2a.text: The tractor owner arrives with rope, coffee, and absolutely no interest in payment.
strings.return.village_return_event_2b.text: The mobile shop skips Tuesday, because locally, Tuesday has quietly become Wednesday.
